notes.meaning: The writer has made a real choice. He has picked God's way, the way of truth, over every false path. Matthew Henry calls this way of living for God the only true road to happiness. He keeps God's rules in front of him, the way a child copies a writing lesson or a builder follows a plan.

"Cling" is a strong word. It means to stick fast, almost to be glued. It is the same word used in verse 25, where his soul clings to the dust. Now he clings to God's word instead. He asks God not to let him do anything that would bring him shame, and not to turn away his service. He also asks God not to let his hope come to nothing.

To "run" means to obey eagerly and gladly, not slowly or grudgingly. God "enlarges the heart" when He fills it with wisdom, love and joy. He also sets it free from the things that hold it back. A heart God has made bigger can move freely in His ways.

differ.view: No one can choose good or make progress until God enlarges the heart. The heart cannot do it by itself. God gives both the desire and the strength.
It should read "because You will enlarge my heart." God cleans the heart and clears the path, and then the believer runs and grows every day.
God starts by enlarging the heart, and the believer answers by running, so the two work together. This is not salvation earned by works.

notes.meaning: He asks God Himself to be his teacher. He wants more than the words of God's rules. He wants to know how to live them out in his own life. He knows he cannot keep going "to the end" of his life unless God teaches him again and again and leads him on.

He asks for understanding that only God can give, the kind His Spirit gives. With it he will obey with his whole heart. That means real love on the inside, not just good behavior on the outside. He will not split his love between God and the world.

First he asked God to teach his mind. Now he asks God to move his will, so he will actually walk in God's ways. He gives God a reason: he already delights in that path. So he asks God to finish the good work He has started in him.

He asks God to bend his heart toward His word and away from greed. Greed is singled out because it fights hardest against God's word and is a root of many other sins. The word here means gain taken at someone else's cost, or plain selfishness. Love for God grows as love for the world is pulled out.

"Worthless things" are the empty prizes of this world, like riches, fame and pleasure. What the eyes stare at, the heart soon loves. A traveler who stops to gaze at everything never gets far. So he asks God to turn his eyes away and to make him lively and eager again through His word.

He asks God to make His promises come true for him. God's promises are meant to lead people to reverence Him, which means to honor Him with deep respect and awe. He comes to God as a servant who belongs to Him.

He fears disgrace. Some think he means the shame of falling away from God because he is weak. Others think he means a hidden sin coming to light, or unfair insults from enemies. Either way, he asks God to keep him from dishonoring God's name. He trusts God because God's judgments are good.

He longs to know God's rules better and to keep them more fully. He asks God to give him new life, as God has faithfully promised. When God puts a longing like this in someone, He will also give the power to follow it through.
He asks for God's steady love and His salvation, which means His rescue. Salvation comes from God's mercy and love, not from anything we have earned. He leans on the promise God has already made.

Some people mocked him for trusting God. When God keeps His promise, he will have an answer for them. Trusting God's word gives him courage. In the end it will be clear that trusting God was never in vain.

He prays that God's true word will always be ready on his lips. He wants to speak up for God and never be too afraid or ashamed to do it. Even if he sometimes fails, he asks God not to take the word from him completely. His hope rests on what God has said.
He promises to keep God's law always. He means every day, without slipping back, for the rest of his life and on into eternity. It is God keeping his heart in faith that makes him able to go on.

"Freedom" here is literally "a wide, open place." Serving sin is slavery, but serving God is true freedom. Someone who follows God's word is not caught in traps. He obeys because he wants to, not because he is forced, and he walks with courage.

He will speak boldly about God's word even in front of kings, who often look down on godly talk. We should never be ashamed of our faith, whoever is listening. Lutherans later used this verse as the motto of the Augsburg Confession, an early Lutheran statement of faith.
He doesn't just agree that God's commands are good. He enjoys them because he loves them. The more we delight in serving God, the closer we come to what we are aiming for.

Lifting the hands shows deep longing, as people do in prayer. It also pictures reaching out to take hold of God's commands and putting all his strength into keeping them. He also thinks about God's word carefully and often.

"Remember" does not mean God might forget. It is how someone asks God to keep His promise. God gave the promise, and God also gave him the hope he has in it. So he can boldly ask God to do what He said.

In his suffering, his comfort is that God's promise has brought him back to life. God's word had made him alive and eager before, so he can lean on it now. If God's word makes us holy, it has enough in it to steady us in every situation.
Proud people laughed at him for his faith. Still, he did not turn even a little from God's law. A traveler keeps walking even when the dogs bark at him.

He remembers how God acted in the past. God showed mercy to His people and brought justice on those who harmed them. That memory comforts him because God has not changed. What God did before promises He will act again.

The word for "rage" pictures a burning heat. He is upset not because the wicked hurt him, but because they throw away God's law and dishonor God. His feeling mixes hatred of their sin, zeal for God's glory, and dread of the judgment coming on them.

"The house of my pilgrimage" means this life. Here we are travelers passing through, not settled at home. Travelers sing to make the road feel shorter. In the same way, God's word is his song, and it cheers him along the way.

At night, while others sleep or are afraid, he thinks about God's name. God's name means who God is, what He has said, and what He has done. Remembering God at night helps him keep God's law during the day.

Keeping God's ways has become his settled habit and his share in life. Some read it as: all these blessings came to him because he obeyed. Others read it as: obeying God is a reward in itself. Those who put God first find they have gained a great deal.

A "portion" is a person's share or inheritance. Others want worldly wealth, but he wants God Himself, as the priests of Israel did who had no land of their own. Because God is his portion, he has promised to keep God's words. Grace comes first, and obedience grows out of it.

He has pleaded for God's favor with his whole heart. He does not demand it as something owed to him. He humbly asks for mercy, meaning forgiveness and help to do better. He bases his request on God's promise, not on anything he has earned.

He looked carefully at how he was living. Adam Clarke compares it to someone sewing fine embroidery, who turns the cloth over to check every stitch. Seeing where he had gone wrong, he turned his feet back to God's word. Real change begins with honest thinking and has to end in actually turning back.
